resources.name: Chat App — Ticket 07 (Webhook)
resources.description: External webhook message ingestion (ticket 07), HMAC-SHA256 signed. Unlike the other collections, the '03 - Webhook Tests' folder cannot use env-var templating for the request bodies: Insomnia can't compute an HMAC signature inline, so each signature is precomputed for the EXACT body text sitting next to it. If you edit a body, or the fixture conversation_id changes, you must recompute the signature by hand — see backend/README.md's Webhook section for the recipe (HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body bytes, keyed by WEBHOOK_HMAC_SECRET, hex-encoded).

resources.name: 01 - Auth (fixture users, reference only)
resources.description: These created the fixture conversation that '03 - Webhook Tests' is hardcoded against (conversation_id 2811b4a5-60d9-4f81-b899-3e78012b29b9, participants insomnia-a@example.com / insomnia-b@example.com). Already run once against the local DB — re-running Register will 409 (duplicate email) unless the DB was reset. Kept here so the fixture is reproducible from scratch if needed.

resources.name: 02 - Setup (create the fixture conversation)
resources.description: Also already run once. If you re-create it, the response `id` will be a NEW UUID — you must then recompute every signature in '03 - Webhook Tests' against that new conversation_id (they're hardcoded, not templated).

resources.name: Create 1:1 conversation (A -> B)
resources.description: Expect 201. Copy response `id` -> env `conversation_id` for reference. The fixture value baked into '03 - Webhook Tests' is 2811b4a5-60d9-4f81-b899-3e78012b29b9.

resources.name: 03 - Webhook Tests (ticket 07) — hardcoded bodies + signatures
resources.description: Every body+signature pair below is pinned to conversation_id 2811b4a5-60d9-4f81-b899-3e78012b29b9 and secret 'change-me' (backend/.env's WEBHOOK_HMAC_SECRET). Run '5. Unknown conversation_id' anytime (no fixture dependency); the other four require the fixture conversation from folders 01-02 to already exist in the DB.

resources.name: 1. Valid signature -> 201 persisted + delivered
resources.description: Expect: 201, response echoes sender_id=null, sender_type=external, source_label=Insomnia Test.

resources.name: 2. Missing X-Signature header -> 401
resources.description: No X-Signature header sent at all. Expect: 401, no message persisted.

resources.name: 3. Invalid X-Signature (garbage) -> 401
resources.description: X-Signature is 64 zero characters - well-formed hex but wrong. Expect: 401, no message persisted.

resources.name: 4. Tampered body -> 401
resources.description: X-Signature below is valid for body {"conversation_id": "2811b4a5-60d9-4f81-b899-3e78012b29b9", "body": "original message"} but the body actually sent says 'tampered message' instead. Expect: 401 — the signature no longer matches the bytes sent.

resources.name: 5. Unknown conversation_id -> 404
resources.description: Valid signature, but conversation_id 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 doesn't exist. Expect: 404. No fixture dependency — works even without folders 01-02.

resources.name: 6. Custom message (UTF-8 source_label) -> 201
resources.description: Ad-hoc manual test with a non-ASCII source_label (accented 'é' + trailing space), to confirm the signature check works over UTF-8-encoded bytes, not just ASCII. Expect: 201, response echoes the body/source_label verbatim, delivered live to any connected participant.

body.text: {"conversation_id": "2811b4a5-60d9-4f81-b899-3e78012b29b9", "body": "Hello from Insomnia", "source_label": "Esse é um teste de webhook "}
